subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw accept additive `first-progress` and `startup-failed` lifecycle phases as the core sub-agent startup contract, or solve the startup ambiguity through a different internal/session-state mechanism?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the requested fix creates a new core event surface that affects gateway lifecycle projection, agent waits, SDK normalization, docs, and subagent consumers.

options.title: Adopt additive lifecycle phases
options.body: Rebase and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77415 or an equivalent PR so the new phases are wired through all lifecycle consumers with proof.

options.title: Use an internal-only failure projection
options.body: Keep the public lifecycle contract unchanged and instead teach subagent/gateway state projections to classify startup aborts without new event phases.

options.title: Decline the lifecycle contract
options.body: Close the request as not planned and keep the current timeout/abort semantics, accepting that startup aborts can remain ambiguous.

recommendation.title: Adopt additive lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Rebase and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77415 or an equivalent PR so the new phases are wired through all lifecycle consumers with proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across subagent lifecycle, terminal outcome, gateway projection, and compatibility boundaries where this history shows repeated ownership.
